title: 256 9-round BDK+10: aes256-9r-xor-cp-full-bdk2010

target.description: 9-round AES-256 variant starting at round 0, with source omitted-final-MixColumns convention. Section 4.1.3 recovers consecutive subkeys K7,K8 and reverses the AES-256 key schedule.

setting.key_relation: K-prime = K XOR (b,b,b,b,a,0,a,0), where alpha is any nonzero byte, beta is its unique probability-2^-6 AES S-box output difference, a=(alpha,0,0,0)^T and b=MC((beta,0,0,0)^T).
setting.plaintext_model: Source CP accounting at 2^38; plaintext identities, paired related-key queries and total oracle calls are distinguished in the resource note.
assumptions: The related-subkey relation, where used, is stronger than a fixed XOR master-key relation but all expanded subkeys remain consistent with their master key.

time.note: Source-native heterogeneous accounting: acquisition is 2^39 9-round AES-256 encryptions; processing is 2^21 * 2^8 * 2^16 = 2^45 simple table lookups. A 9-round encryption uses 9*16=144 approximately 2^7 S-box operations, and the source says processing is likely faster. The headline exponent 39 is not an exact sum in one interchangeable unit.

data.note: 2^38 distinct chosen plaintext identities are encrypted under both keys, giving 2^39 total encryption queries and 2^38 ciphertext pairs. Preserve Table 1 native data convention.

memory.note: Table 1 states 2^32 without a storage unit. Section 4.1.3 calls RAM negligible; footnote 2 streams the ciphertext data on disk while each working set fits 1 MByte. Observation B separately allocates 2^17 bytes to the DDT. Retain all storage layers; neither 2^32 bytes nor zero RAM is justified.

preprocessing.note: Section 4.1.2 DDT setup; 2^17 bytes for this auxiliary table, separate from data storage.

success.description: Section 4.1.3 states about 57% full attack success, controlled by four or more right-pair suggestions in step 2(c), with success increased by using additional pairs. Recover K^7 and K^8 and invert the AES-256 key schedule to recover all 256 master-key bits.

evidence.locator: PDF p.3 Table 1; pp.5–6 key relation; pp.9–13 Sections 4.1.2–4.2, full-key completion and accounting.
evidence.interpretation: Primary table and defining text checked. Unknown costs are retained rather than preventing extraction.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.6–12 / printed pp.304–310 Sections 4.1–4.1.3, especially p.9 Observation B and p.12 complexity plus footnote 2; p.3 Table 1 row 3.
evidence.interpretation: Independent complete 21-page exact-edition audit, frozen raw-first inventory and bounded forward/version checks through 2026-10-10. Native resource units and author-reported endpoint preserved; finite component checks are not attack reproduction.

limitations: Table 1 memory 2^32 has no stated unit. Section 4.1.3 calls working RAM negligible (fits 1 MByte), with data on disk. These describe different storage layers and are not collapsed into a single byte claim.

The complete inspected 2010 edition contains ten attack configurations. A distinct author-hosted draft contains an additional multi-key variant; its original PDF version/hash remains an explicit separate evidence task and is not merged into this source.
